subject: product_goal
statement: The goal is for new employees to give their information once, so that HR stops chasing them for the same information several times. The stakeholder agreed to this goal.

anchors.quote: We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for the same information three times.

judge_note: Goal is stated by Leo (interviewer), and Anna's 'Yes, please' responds to a different question; her explicit agreement to the goal is not clearly shown.

subject: current_process
statement: Today HR uses a Word document and an Excel file, then types everything into the receiving parties' portals by hand. Last month this took a full afternoon for two new hires.

anchors.quote: I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand.
Last month I spent a full afternoon on two new hires.

judge_note: Word, Excel, manual typing into 'the portals' and the afternoon for two hires are supported, but 'receiving parties' portals' is an embellishment.

subject: hiring_volume
statement: Muster AG hires around twenty people a year, more in summer. It has about 150 employees, mostly in Zurich.

anchors.quote: Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.

subject: source_tax_questionnaire
statement: Source tax takes HR the most time. HR does not know up front who must answer the source tax questions, so today it sends the whole questionnaire to everybody, and Swiss employees get annoyed.

anchors.quote: So I send the whole questionnaire to everybody, and the Swiss people get annoyed, and they call me.

subject: source_tax_questionnaire
statement: Source tax questions should only be asked to employees who are subject to source tax, not to everybody.

anchors.quote: Because I never know up front who has to answer those questions.
the Swiss people get annoyed, and they call me.

judge_note: Reasonable inference: she doesn't know who needs to answer, and sending to everybody is the pain.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: First version: all non-Swiss employees (anyone without a Swiss passport) are subject to source tax.

anchors.quote: All the non-Swiss employees. Simple as that. If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: HR uses the Zurich tariff calculator on the canton's website to get the tariff code, clicking through it with the employee's answers.

anchors.quote: I use the Zurich calculator on the canton's website. The one that gives you the tariff code.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: For now, the Zurich calculator is used for every employee subject to source tax. The stakeholder knows this is not exactly how it works, and the interviewer agreed to keep it this way.

anchors.quote: For everybody I use Zurich, by the way. I know it's not exactly how it works, but that's what we do for now.

judge_note: She uses Zurich for everybody, not only those subject to source tax (though only they would use it); interviewer 'keep that for now' is supported.

subject: address
statement: HR needs the employee's full address: street, house number, postcode, town and country.

anchors.quote: Yes, I need the address, obviously. The full address. Street, number, postcode, town, country.

subject: address
statement: The address must be complete, because HR posts many documents to employees. It is a normal postal address, as you would write it on an envelope, with no extra parts.

anchors.quote: We post a lot of documents to people, so it has to be complete.
No, no. Just a normal address, the way you would write it on an envelope.

subject: photo
statement: The stakeholder would like the form to ask for a photo of the employee for badges. Today reception takes badge photos with a phone and they come out badly.

anchors.quote: Oh, that would be so nice, actually. For the badges.
Could the form ask for a photo?

subject: photo
statement: No photo will be collected for now, because security is changing the badge system next year. The topic will be revisited next year.

anchors.quote: Let's not do that now. Forget the photo for the moment, we'll talk about it next year.

subject: pension_fund
statement: Muster AG's pension fund is Pensionskasse Muster. It has an old portal, and HR will send screenshots of it.

anchors.quote: We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old.
I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call

subject: first_working_day
statement: HR needs the employee's first working day for the pension fund. It is the most important item, and HR asks the employee to confirm it because it changes often.

anchors.quote: I need their first working day. That's the number one thing, and I ask them to confirm it, because it moves more often than you'd think.

judge_note: First working day and confirmation are supported, but it is said to be the number one thing generally, and 'for the pension fund' is reasonable given context; 'changes often' is supported.

subject: first_working_day
statement: The first working day often changes, for example when new hires negotiate leaving their old employer a week earlier.

anchors.quote: People negotiate with their old employer, they get out a week earlier.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: First version: pension fund insurance starts on the first day of the month after the first working day. Example: a first working day of 15.03 gives an insurance start of 01.04.

anchors.quote: because insurance starts on the first of the following month. So for her that was the first of April

judge_note: Insurance starts on the first of the following month; the 15 March to 1 April example is given.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Exception: if the first working day is exactly the first day of a month, insurance starts on that same day.

anchors.quote: Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day.

judge_note: T-028 states that starting exactly on the first means that day.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Final rule: the insurance start date is derived from the first working day. If the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day. Otherwise it starts on the 1st of the following month. The employee is not asked for it.

anchors.quote: because insurance starts on the first of the following month.
Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day.

judge_note: The derivation rule is supported, but 'the employee is not asked for it' is not stated in these units.

subject: first_working_day
statement: Incident: Julia moved her first working day to 15 March, HR did not update it, and the fund ended up with a wrong insurance start date (it should have been 1 April). This led to an unfriendly letter and took weeks to fix. It shows that the insurance start date must follow the latest confirmed first working day.

anchors.quote: She moved her first working day to the 15th of March, and I didn't update it.
I got a very unfriendly letter.

judge_note: The incident is supported, but 'it should have been 1 April' is fine while the 'must follow the latest confirmed first working day' conclusion is an inference; the units also say 'I had entered something else', not specifically that HR failed to update the insurance date, though she did say she didn't update it.

subject: civil_status
statement: The pension fund asks for the employee's civil status.

anchors.quote: Yes, the civil status. They ask for that.

judge_note: Anna says the fund asks for civil status.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: If the employee is married, the pension fund wants the date of birth of the husband or wife.

anchors.quote: And if someone is married, they want the date of birth of the husband or wife.

judge_note: Stated in T-032.

subject: civil_status
statement: Civil status options, from the stakeholder's memory and not confirmed: Single, Married, Divorced, and she thinks Widowed. She deferred to the pension fund screenshots for the actual list.

anchors.quote: I'd have to look. You'll see it in the screenshots. Single, married, divorced, I think widowed.

judge_note: Options are from memory and she defers to screenshots.

subject: civil_status
statement: One current employee (Daniel, in finance) is in a registered partnership. He was entered before the current HR manager's time.

anchors.quote: we do have one colleague in a registered partnership. Daniel, in finance.

judge_note: Daniel in finance is in a registered partnership and was entered before her time (T-036).

subject: civil_status
statement: Unresolved: how the pension fund's screen handles a registered partnership, and whether the fund wants the partner's details.

anchors.quote: I honestly don't know what the fund's screen does in that case, or if they want the partner's details too.

judge_note: Anna explicitly says she doesn't know what the fund's screen does or whether partner details are wanted.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Correction: employees with a C permit are not subject to source tax and are treated like Swiss nationals (example: Maria, Portuguese with a C permit). So the rule becomes non-Swiss, except C permit holders. Asked if that was everything, the stakeholder answered only 'I think so'.

anchors.quote: So, not the people with a C permit. They're treated like Swiss people for this.
Okay, so non-Swiss, but not with a C permit.

judge_note: C permit correction, Maria example and the 'I think so' answer are all in the units.

subject: metrics
statement: The stakeholder offered to get numbers on how long the process takes from their payroll person.

anchors.quote: Do you want some numbers on how long this takes? I could get that for you from our payroll person.

judge_note: Offer in T-040.

subject: it_equipment
statement: Laptops and IT equipment are out of scope. IT has its own process.

anchors.quote: IT does laptops, they have their own process, keep them out of this, please.

judge_note: T-042 says IT has its own process and to keep laptops out.

subject: permit_reminder
statement: The stakeholder would love the form to remind employees to bring their permit, because half of them forget. Not decided: the interviewer deferred the wording to later.

anchors.quote: What I would love is if the form could remind people to bring their permit. Half of them forget.
We can look at the wording later.

judge_note: Wish in T-042; wording deferred in T-043.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: For married employees, the source tax calculator asks different questions, for example whether the husband or wife works.

anchors.quote: It changes the questions in the calculator, yes. Whether the husband or wife works.

judge_note: T-044 says it changes calculator questions, e.g. whether the spouse works.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Addition: an employee married to someone who is Swiss or holds a C permit, and who lives in Switzerland, is not subject to source tax. Example: Tomás, Brazilian with a B permit, whose Swiss wife lives with him in Winterthur.

anchors.quote: If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
Brazilian, B permit, but his wife is Swiss, and they live in Winterthur. So no source tax for him.

judge_note: T-044 gives the rule and the Tomás example.

subject: spouse_details
statement: To decide on source tax, HR needs the spouse's nationality, the spouse's permit (if they have one), and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland.

anchors.quote: So you need to know about the spouse as well.
Yes. Their nationality, their permit if they have one, and that they live here.

subject: spouse_details
statement: Spouse nationality, permit and residence are only needed for married employees whose own status would otherwise make them subject to source tax: non-Swiss, no C permit, living in Switzerland. The spouse permit is only needed if the spouse is not Swiss.

anchors.quote: it also changes who has to do it at all.
Their nationality, their permit if they have one, and that they live here.

judge_note: Scoping to otherwise-subject employees and the 'permit only if spouse not Swiss' detail are reasonable readings but not stated.

subject: spouse_details
statement: Today HR checks the spouse case by hand and collects spouse details by email, which takes a long time.

anchors.quote: I always have to check that one by hand.
I ask them by email, and it takes forever.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Addition: employees who live abroad and work in Switzerland are always subject to source tax, whatever their nationality. Example: Stefan is Swiss, lives in Konstanz, and is still subject.

anchors.quote: Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.
And there it doesn't matter what passport you have, by the way.
So someone living abroad and working here always does it?

subject: cross_border_employees
statement: Some employees live across the border, for example in Konstanz (Germany) and in Liechtenstein.

anchors.quote: Stefan lives in Konstanz, and there's a woman in the warehouse who lives in Liechtenstein.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: For employees living abroad, the source tax calculator asks more questions. Germany has its own forms, which the stakeholder cannot name. The interviewer said the calculator will define these questions.

anchors.quote: And with them the calculator gets much more complicated, there are more questions.
Germany has its own forms, I can never remember what they're called.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Consolidated final rule. (1) An employee whose home address is outside Switzerland is subject to source tax, whatever their nationality. (2) An employee living in Switzerland who is Swiss or holds a C permit is not subject. (3) An employee living in Switzerland who is non-Swiss without a C permit is not subject if married to a spouse who is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland. (4) Otherwise the employee is subject. The stakeholder hedged on completeness ('I think that's it').

anchors.quote: If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.
So, not the people with a C permit. They're treated like Swiss people for this.
If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.

judge_note: Reasonable consolidation of the stated rules.

subject: nationality
statement: The employee's nationality is needed to decide whether they are subject to source tax.

anchors.quote: If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.

subject: permit_type
statement: Non-Swiss employees' permit type (e.g. B permit, C permit) is needed to decide whether they are subject to source tax.

anchors.quote: She has a C permit. So, not the people with a C permit.

subject: residence_country
statement: 'Lives here' in the source tax rules means living in Switzerland. The employee's country of residence can be taken from the country of the home address.

anchors.quote: Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.

judge_note: 'Lives here' = Switzerland is supported, but nothing in these units links residence to the home address country.

subject: timeline
statement: The stakeholder asked when the product can be delivered. The interviewer will reply this week, after reviewing the screenshots.

anchors.quote: Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.

subject: pension_portal
statement: The source is the 'Register new employee' page of the Pensionskasse Muster employer portal, used by the employer Muster AG to register new insured employees.
judge_note: Page and portal are shown, but 'employer Muster AG' and 'insured employees' are not stated explicitly.

subject: first_name
statement: The pension fund registration requires the employee's first name (text input, marked required).

subject: last_name
statement: The pension fund registration requires the employee's last name (text input, marked required).

subject: date_of_birth
statement: The pension fund registration requires the employee's date of birth (text input, marked required).

subject: date_of_birth
statement: The employee's date of birth is entered in the format DD.MM.YYYY.

subject: residence_canton
statement: The pension fund registration requires a canton (dropdown in the Employee section, marked required); the portal does not label whether it is the residence or work canton.
judge_note: Required dropdown in Employee section; no residence/work label visible.

subject: residence_canton
statement: The Canton dropdown offers exactly these 26 options: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich. There is no option for living outside Switzerland.
judge_note: 26 options listed; no abroad option.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: The pension fund registration requires an insurance start date (text input in the Insurance section, marked required).

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: The insurance start date is entered as DD.MM.YYYY and must be the 1st of a month.

anchors.quote: DD.MM.YYYY. Must be the 1st of a month.

subject: civil_status
statement: The pension fund registration requires the employee's civil status (dropdown, marked required).

subject: civil_status
statement: The Civil status dropdown offers exactly these options: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: The pension fund registration has a 'Spouse's date of birth' field (text input) that is marked required when it is shown.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: The spouse's date of birth is entered in the format DD.MM.YYYY.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: The 'Spouse's date of birth' field appears only when civil status is 'Married': it is shown in screenshots 05 and 07 (civil status Married) and absent in screenshot 04 (civil status Single) and in the empty forms (01, 02, 03, 06).
judge_note: Absence in screenshots 01, 02, 03, 06 and 04 is not shown by the units given (only 04 label list lacks it); conditional-only-on-Married is a reasonable inference but the empty-form claims are unverified.

subject: required_validation
statement: Submitting the form with required fields empty shows the banner 'Please correct the highlighted fields.', highlights each empty field and shows a per-field error of the form '<Field> is required.' (First name, Last name, Date of birth, Canton, Insurance start date, Civil status).
judge_note: Banner, highlights and per-field errors all present in S06.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: When civil status is Married and the spouse's date of birth is left empty, the portal blocks registration with the error 'Spouse's date of birth is required.'

anchors.quote: Spouse's date of birth is required.

subject: residence_canton
statement: The Canton dropdown only lists Swiss cantons; it is unclear what to enter for an employee who lives abroad (e.g. a cross-border commuter living in Germany), and whether the field means the residence canton or the work canton.
judge_note: Reasonable inference: only Swiss cantons listed and no label clarifies residence vs work.

subject: civil_status
statement: No screenshot shows the form with civil status Divorced or Widowed, so it is unknown whether any extra fields (e.g. spouse data) appear for those values; the list also has no option such as registered partnership or separated, and it is unclear how such cases are to be registered.
judge_note: List has only four options, and screenshots shown include only Single and Married; reasonable open-question reading.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: The portal requires an insurance start date that is the 1st of a month, but does not say how it relates to the employee's first working day (e.g. whether a mid-month start rounds to the same or the next month's 1st); the derivation rule is open.

anchors.quote: DD.MM.YYYY. Must be the 1st of a month.

judge_note: Hint only states 1st of month; no relation to first working day is shown.

subject: date_validation
statement: No screenshot shows the error for a badly formatted date or for an insurance start date that is not the 1st of a month, so the wording and behaviour of these errors are unknown.

anchors.quote: DD.MM.YYYY. Must be the 1st of a month.

judge_note: The units show only a hint (DD.MM.YYYY, must be 1st of month) and a required error, with no format or non-1st-date error visible, but the claim that no screenshot shows them goes beyond these units, which cover only one screenshot.
